description:
## Problem
The gate table on #4322 missed inputs that change SF 1 bytes. Head ea09ba98c4 now gates `benchbox/core/tsbs_devops/schema.py`, `benchbox/core/joinorder/schema.py` and the CoffeeShop seed files, and docs/internal/generator-volume-gate.md lists shared utility modules, including `coffeeshop_seed_loader.py`, as ungated limits.

## Owner decision
2026-11-20 (choice dialog, 13:25Z), gate_utils = "seed-loader-and-limit": gate only `coffeeshop_seed_loader.py`; keep the rest as a documented limit.

## Change
On the #4322 branch: add `coffeeshop_seed_loader.py` to the gate table and the CI path filter and remove it from the documented limits. Leave the other shared utility modules as documented limits. No import-closure test.

## Decision gates
None beyond the decision above. Nothing else is added to or removed from the gate.

## Verification rubric
Pass: the table, the CI filter and the doc agree and name `coffeeshop_seed_loader.py` as gated; the existing gate tests pass with a case for that path; the three inputs gated in ea09ba98c4 are still gated.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
Accepted by the owner in the choice dialog: the agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
Review threads: the accepted text also said the agent never resolves a thread. Asked afterwards which rule applies, the owner chose: "The morning rule: I may resolve a thread once the bot has reviewed the new head and did not raise the finding again." ('I' is the agent.) So the agent pushes the fix and replies, and resolves a thread only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise that finding again.
